<reason>Side A won a close, high-quality clash by holding the proposition to its text: multi-author opt-in is a de facto ban, including on commercial security classifiers, while leaving retention, review, and profiling standing. Side B’s appropriation frame and “twelve people wrote it” close were powerful, and CON’s admission that it would still train after twelve silences was a real hit, but PRO never resolved motion scope or showed why a veto incumbents can buy beats harm duties.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Q1-on-the-text plus R2 use of PRO’s “other rules can reach them,” turning uncollectable yeses into an owned ban whose load-bearing protections are borrowed.</best_rebuttal>
